_comment: Typed registry of the addresses in source/offsets/off_1360.c.
One entry per field. `namespace` is what the value may be added to; it is the
one thing that must never be inferred from the value's magnitude alone.
`class` is the evidence class from the table's header (KNOWN_STATIC,
`provenance` names the artifact, `verified_by` the check that re-derives it.
Enforced by tools/check_offset_registry.py, which fails when this file and the
C table disagree or when a value violates its namespace.

entries.provenance: resolved from the ELF 1360linux.elf published by Sonic ISO (sha256 e51a0298cb2c97b7…) and cross-validated three ways. (1) Field mapping: the ELF carries 28 per-firmware offset tables copied into env_offset by set_offsets(); reading the WiFi fields at struct +0x128/+0x130 -- the very displacements dump_ps5_wifi_firmware tests before dumping -- reproduces the known values of six firmwares exactly (3.00 0x1274460/492304, 3.10 0x1274490/492304, 4.50 0x1392FC0/493000, 5.00 0x142E2B0/493532, 6.00 0x1455C00/494536, 7.61 0x1445800/497636), and the struct order matches offsets.h (IOMMU_SOFTC, VM_VMID, VM_PMAP, DATA_BASE_GVMSPACE, ACPIGBL_FACS, IDT …) with six anchors landing exactly where they belong. (2) Its 13.60 table agrees with our independently resolved values: FUN_TRANSMITTER_CONTROL 0xC0EAA0, FUN_MP3_INVOKE 0xA12D30, KERNEL_CFI_CHECK 0x44F8C0, IDT 0x3BB4300, DATA_BASE_GVMSPACE 0x3BAA570. (3) Capture checks: the qword at IOMMU_SOFTC is a canonical kernel pointer (0xffffff8007568000); the WiFi region starts with 01000000, contains ARM firmware code (e59ff01c x8) and has clean boundaries
entries.verified_by: ELF reverse engineering + 6-firmware validation + capture check 2026-10-16

entries.provenance: aligned: the working loader carries VMID 0x1EC in BOTH its 13.60 and its 12.00 tables, while 0x1E4 appears only on 3.00-4.51 (and the field is left 0/'not needed' on 5.00-11.00). Ours was a stale value inherited from older firmware

dispute settled: the working 13.60 loader carries 0x1D8 for this field, the same value we derived, against the payload SDK's 0x2E8. The SDK value is therefore for a different structure or build; ours is corroborated by an independently written loader that boots

corroborated, two sources: (1) HV-Bypass-13.60 GVMSPACE_DRIFT_1360.md measured it in a live 16 MB .data dump as 0x2EEA570 kdata-relative (= 0x3BAA570 ktext-relative) anchored on the IDT with the gap 0x9D90 stable across 11.60/12.70/13.60; (2) our capture: the IDT at the same anchor (0x3BB4300) re-verified 256/256 gates with selector 0x20, and 0x3BB4300-0x3BAA570 = 0x9D90. Namespace: KDATA_REL, which is what this registry means for an address beyond the text image (it was STRUCT_OFF, a small struct offset, so the checker would have refused any real value)
0x2D39000 is Byepervisor's KERNEL_SYM_DATA_CAVE: data, not executable code

entries.verified_by: tools/verify_off_1360_dump.py (entry shape only, identity not proven)

entries.provenance: aligned to the working loader. It is a vmmcall wrapper (mov eax,6 ; vmmcall ; stores results through r8/r9), which matches the ABI our shellcode declares: hv_iommu_set_buffers(cb2_pa, cb3_pa, ...). Our previous 0x4FABD0 is an IOMMU-DRIVER function (it references 'iommu io', 'iommu bsf', 'iommu_pci_attach'), the wrong side for a field named HV_iommu
aligned to the working loader for the same reason as SET_BUFFERS: the field is the HV-side wrapper, and ours pointed at the driver-side function

aligned to the working 13.60 loader (1360linux.elf, Sonic ISO). Our previous 0xB04440 was derived from the 'smp rendezvous' string xref, but that function has ZERO callers in the kernel - it is the one that prints the string. 0xB03BA0 has six or more callers and is the value two independent sources use. Ours stays recorded as the alternative

no-op function identified: body is push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; pop rbp; ret. The alias sonic.md reports (ktext+0x261e08) is a stub whose jmp rel32 lands exactly on 0xB03960 -- cross-checked by decoding the stub. Supersedes the earlier 'not required, use GAD_RET_TRAMP' disposition: the kernel's own barrier is now identified
the Byepervisor vector runs from startup_mp, not a fixed VMEXIT cave
read only by the legacy prepare_resume() path, which fw >= 0x0800 never calls (docs/BOOT-REQUIREMENTS-1360.md). Not identified in the capture; not needed for the 13.60 path
capture: strict entry holding "cfi_check_fail: data %p, caller %p, callee %p"
this table claims the capture; docs/1360-offsets-from-dump.md lists G_VBIOS as not covered

identified by convergence of two independent methods. (1) Semantics: the thunk 0x39B3B0 is called with edi=0x4C -- DIG1TRANSMITTERCONTROL, the same constant our shellcode passes -- and rsi pointing at a struct built exactly like dig_transmitter_control_parameters_v1_6, from the display code that logs with [av control k] and neighbours the AMD mmDIG1_AFMT_GENERIC_* register names (so those Ethernet 'PMD transmitter' strings are a different subsystem and were rejected). The thunk is jmp 0xC0EAA0; 0xC0EAA0 takes edi as the command and rsi as the params pointer (mov r14d,edi ; mov rbx,rsi), i.e. the documented ABI. (2) Position: 13.20's value 0xC01ED0 plus the locally measured drift +0xCBD0 -- derived from the verified HV_MP_STARTUP_CALL pair 0xC0A310 -> 0xC16EE0 -- lands on exactly 0xC0EAA0. off_1320.c describes the same symbol as a 'generic ATOM exec taking (int cmd, void *params)', which is what 0xC0EAA0 is. 0x39B3B0 is a verified alternative entry (it forwards to the same code)

aligned to the working loader, and flagged as a divergence worth settling on hardware. Their value is the inner command sender; ours 0xA13740 is a 2544-byte function that CALLS it and that carries the '[MP3] failed to init message thread' string. A signature string tied the name to 0xA13740, the empirical boot ties it to 0xA14130; a hardware run will decide. Both are real entries, so the wrong choice fails loudly rather than subtly

identified by convergence, not by a signature string: (1) ABI match -- the function takes three arguments and uses all of them the way our shellcode calls it, mp3_invoke(cmd_id, req, rsp): edi is stored and written into the IPC message (mov r15d,edi ; mov [r14],r15d), rsi is copied in as the request (0x1404 bytes via 0x2590b0), rdx is used at the end (mov rdi,rbx) as the response; it has an entry prologue and a stack canary and returns -22 when an initialised-flag global is not 1; (2) position -- it sits exactly 0xA10 below the verified FUN_MP3_INITIALIZE 0xA13740, and 0xA10 is precisely the distance between the two symbols in the 13.20 table (0xA0B3E0 - 0xA0A9D0); (3) it has no direct caller in .text, which is what an address exported through the boot ABI table looks like. Residual uncertainty: no unique string ties the symbol to the name, so this is weaker than the FUN_MP3_INITIALIZE derivation (which had a signature string)

boot_requirements._comment: Per field: what its absence blocks. boot_minimal = mandatory to reach the kernel entry point; phase_b = mandatory only for the post-resume takeover; optional = absence is handled by the code; none = not read on the 13.60 path. Derived from the call sites in docs/BOOT-REQUIREMENTS-1360.md: main.c skips prepare_resume() for fw >= 0x0800, so the shellcode_kernel_args writers are not on the 13.60 path.
boot_minimal_exceptions: KERNEL_CFI_CHECK: also read by hv_defeat_1360.c (phase-A patch + read-back)

FUN_SMP_NO_RENDEVOUS_BARRIER.why: prepare_sck_args() only; the shellcode can supply a no-op

IOMMU_SOFTC.why: prepare_sck_args() / hw/iommu.c only; IOMMU setup lives in the legacy kernel shellcode

KERNEL_CODE_CAVE.why: prepare_sck_args() (guarded) and the legacy defeat vectors only; 0x2D39000 is kernel data

HV_CODE_CAVE_PA.why: prepare_sck_args() only; the Byepervisor vector runs from startup_mp

FUN_TRANSMITTER_CONTROL.why: prepare_sck_args() only; display bring-up is not on the 13.60 path

FUN_MP3_INITIALIZE.why: prepare_sck_args() only; audio is not on the 13.60 path

FUN_MP3_INVOKE.why: prepare_sck_args() only; audio is not on the 13.60 path

PS5_WIFI_FW_OFFSET.why: dump_device_firmwares() runs for 13.60 but fails gracefully when the offset is 0 (loader.c logs 'Continuing')

DATA_BASE_GVMSPACE.why: read by gpu_init(), which has no caller in this tree

G_VBIOS.why: prepare_sck_args() only; the DISPUTED value is the open item, not the absence
